title: Tener: tengo, tienes, tiene
explanation: Tener means to have. At A0, use tengo for I have, tienes for you have, and recognize tiene for he/she has. Pronunciation: tener = teh-NEHR, tengo = TEHN-goh, tienes = TYEH-nes, tiene = TYEH-neh. Use tener for possessions, as in Tengo un libro. Spanish also uses tener in fixed expressions such as Tengo hambre. A common beginner mistake is translating I am hungry with soy or estoy; for this expression, use tengo hambre.
examples: Tengo un libro. = I have a book.
Ana tiene un libro. = Ana has a book.
Common mistake: Soy hambre. Use Tengo hambre.

title: Basic word order in short sentences
explanation: Very short Spanish sentences often use subject plus verb plus the rest of the idea. At A0, keep familiar patterns intact: Me llamo Ana, Soy de Madrid, Tengo un libro, and Ana tiene un libro. Do not rearrange the words randomly; Spanish word order can vary later, but these beginner patterns should be memorized as stable chunks.
examples: Me llamo Ana. = My name is Ana.
Soy de Madrid. = I am from Madrid.
Tengo un libro. = I have a book.
Ana tiene un libro. = Ana has a book.
